source_metadata.title: SkillTrace: Multi-Trace Provenance Auditing for LLM-Agent Skill Reuse
source_metadata.source_type: arXiv preprint / AI software systems benchmark study
source_metadata.input_file: SkillTrace Multi-Trace Provenance Auditing for LLM-Agent Skill Reuse - 2608.05204v2.pdf

atoms.canonical_statement: The study evaluates whether a multi-trace, provenance-attributed auditor can detect transformed reuse of LLM-agent skills, distinguish it from same-function independent similarity, support ecosystem discovery, and scale through cached trace comparison.
A skill pair is treated as a reuse candidate when the candidate preserves at least one concrete provenance trace of the reference beyond similarity expected from same-function independent skills.
SKILLTRACE is explicitly framed as a provenance-auditing and forensic-triage system, not a legal infringement detector.

SKILLTRACE extracts three separate provenance traces—Expression, Implementation, and Operational—so that preserved wording, executable realization, and host-aware operational design can be audited independently.

The Expression Trace is deterministically extracted from natural-language substrates including metadata, descriptions, when-to-use fields, instructions, reference files, and assets after removing common stopwords and scaffold boilerplate.
The Implementation Trace uses a language-agnostic token representation over inline code, support scripts, shell commands, API calls, configuration schemas, and command-line interfaces.
The Operational Trace is represented as a typed Skill Operational Graph (SOG) intended to capture agent-host execution design rather than only surface text or code.
A SOG is defined by normalized operational blocks, an activation signature, procedure structure, and resource-flow structure.
Each operational block is normalized into five fields: action, object role, tool role, inputs, and outputs.
The SOG schema uses frozen closed vocabularies for actions, object roles, tool roles, activation contexts, and relation types, with rare lexical variants merged into coarser roles.
The SOG Activation view captures user intent, required context, host-facing trigger conditions, and the first operational blocks needed for that context.
The SOG Procedure view captures ordering, dependencies, branches, fallback paths, failure handling, and tool-call order across operational blocks.
The SOG Resource-Flow view captures tool, resource, and artifact dependencies such as support files, external services, APIs, intermediate outputs, generated reports, and validation artifacts.
Operational traces are extracted once at ingestion with an LLM constrained to a frozen SOG schema; the normalized graphs are cached and versioned, and pairwise audits make no further LLM calls.
Expression similarity is token Jaccard overlap between normalized natural-language token sets, with matched tokens retained as evidence pointers.

Implementation similarity is token Jaccard overlap between normalized implementation-token sets; when either skill lacks sufficient implementation substrate, this trace is marked not applicable rather than scored as zero.
Operational similarity combines block, activation, procedure, and resource-flow similarity with fixed weights 0.30, 0.10, 0.40, and 0.20 respectively.
BlockSim uses maximum one-to-one matching between normalized operational blocks plus a weak longest-common-subsequence term over normalized block order.
ActSim compares compact activation signatures by normalized role overlap and is down-weighted because same-function independent skills may share generic trigger conditions.
ProcSim combines typed procedure-edge Jaccard with sequence alignment over normalized block order.
ResSim compares directed typed block-resource dependency edges after node-label normalization without imposing a global resource-flow order.

Each trace threshold is calibrated as the 95th percentile of its score distribution on N1 same-function strict negatives, corresponding to a per-trace 5% false-positive calibration without positive examples.

The final SkillTrace score is the maximum applicable trace similarity divided by its calibrated threshold; with the default decision bound beta=1.0, any one trace meeting threshold surfaces the pair for review.
For surfaced pairs, the audit report records the firing trace, raw and calibrated scores, and trace-specific evidence pointers, including matched text/code features or aligned SOG structures.

SKILLTRACE-BENCH is built from 100 public marketplace skill anchors selected to cover diverse task categories, package sizes, and implementation styles while limiting duplicates from the same owner and provenance cluster.

population.label: Public marketplace skill anchors used to construct SKILLTRACE-BENCH

atoms.canonical_statement: SKILLTRACE-BENCH contains 820 positive reuse pairs drawn from observable ecosystem reuse and controlled transformations.

population.label: Positive reuse pairs in SKILLTRACE-BENCH

atoms.canonical_statement: The positive benchmark includes three transformation regimes: repackaging (R1 metadata rewrite, R2 structural reorganization), porting/rewriting (P1 cross-modal port, P2 registry fork, P3 full LLM rewrite), and partial lifting/replacement (L1 implementation lift, L2 code refactor, L3 documentation reuse).
The benchmark negative side contains 751 controls intended to separate provenance-bearing reuse from same-function similarity.

population.label: Negative controls in SKILLTRACE-BENCH

atoms.canonical_statement: N1 strict negatives are same-function but independently implemented real-corpus pairs; mirrors, same-owner reuse, same-provenance clusters, and shared-template-only cases are excluded, and admission requires cross-model agreement on independence.
N2 controls are clean-room skills generated from task metadata without access to the original skill body; N2 is a boundary control and is not used for threshold calibration.

Benchmark inclusion is checked using repository metadata and package structure for observable reuse, cross-model filtering for LLM-generated positives, and manual review of admitted positive and negative pairs.
RepoClone-Jaccard and RepoClone-ssdeep serve as package-level baselines by flattening repository contents and computing token Jaccard or ssdeep fuzzy-hash similarity.
Controlled evaluation reports AUROC, precision, recall, F1, per-family mean scores, and detection rates using thresholds calibrated only on N1 strict negatives.

The wild-corpus deployment study does not report AUROC because complete provenance ground truth is unavailable; it instead reports ecosystem findings, detector disagreement, and manual validation of sampled candidates.

atoms.canonical_statement: Manual wild-corpus validation blindly reviewed 200 stratified pairs: 100 SKILLTRACE-surfaced pairs and 100 low-priority controls.

population.label: Stratified wild-corpus pairs selected for blind manual review

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors report that SKILLTRACE-flagged wild pairs consistently contained inspectable reuse evidence aligned with the firing trace, whereas low-priority controls were overwhelmingly independent or unclear and lacked comparable provenance evidence.

The authors conclude that trace-attributed queues surface actionable wild-corpus reuse candidates beyond package-level similarity while remaining triage queues rather than provenance or infringement verdicts.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors conclude that LLM cost is amortized at ingestion and that repeated audits over cached traces are deterministic with zero audit-time token cost.
Some positive benchmark pairs are generated by LLM-assisted transformations, which may introduce model-specific stylistic artifacts despite cross-model generation/judging and manual spot checks.
The benchmark does not cover every future marketplace reuse pattern.
The wild audit covers public registries rather than all commercial or private skill ecosystems and is not presented as a prevalence estimate for all skill markets.
LLM-extracted SOGs can still be noisy or too coarse even with an auditor-controlled, temperature-zero, versioned extraction prompt.
Operational evidence can collide for generic same-function skills, so Operational Trace is calibrated against strict negatives and excluded from the global wild-corpus routing rule.
Implementation Trace is applicable only when both skills contain enough code or command material; code-light skills should not be interpreted as implementation mismatches.
Trace similarity does not establish intent, ownership, license compatibility, protectability, or legal infringement.
Shared templates, common API wrappers, and multi-origin merges can create genuine similarity without a clean one-to-one reuse relation.
Reuse that deliberately targets the detector is outside the current benchmark.

The authors argue that Operational similarity alone should not be treated as a reuse verdict; generic low-information SOG matches belong in an ambiguous review zone and are strongest when corroborated by other traces or distinctive resources.

The paper concludes that multi-trace, calibrated, trace-attributed auditing improves transformed skill-reuse detection over package-level baselines while providing evidence suitable for human review and marketplace triage.

extraction_limitations: No supplementary material, code repository, or external marketplace records were consulted; extraction is limited to the uploaded preprint.

The LiteratureAtom schema is oriented toward primary literature and clinical-style exposure/outcome context; AI benchmark quantitative results are represented using generic method-as-exposure and metric-as-outcome descriptors.
Approximate source language such as “about one hundred” and “about seventy” is preserved as qualitative text rather than converted into false precision.
References were treated as provenance infrastructure and were not atomized.
All atoms remain review_status=needs_review because this run has not received independent human verification.
